dedupe_keys.name: lisflood fp two dimensional hydrodynamic flood inundation model

description: LISFLOOD-FP is a two-dimensional hydrodynamic model for floodplain inundation over complex topography, produced by the University of Bristol's hydrology group as a non-commercial research code. It predicts the water depth in each grid cell at each time step and so simulates flood waves over fluvial, coastal and estuarine floodplains. Version 8 offers a local inertia (ACC) solver with a subgrid channel model, first-order finite volume (FV1) and second-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG2) shallow water solvers, GPU acceleration, and a non-uniform multiwavelet grid (8.1); the solvers suit fluvial and pluvial flooding, and FV1 and DG2 also dam breaks and flows around hydraulic structures. Coverage is any area with a raster terrain model. Version 8.2 (2024) is a free download from Zenodo under GPL-2.0, with documentation and tutorials on the SEAMLESS-WAVE site. Caveats: the ACC solver is not recommended for supercritical flows, DG2 is costly for large areas, and the DG2 and FV1 solvers do not work with the subgrid channel model. Simulation uses: flood hazard mapping, dam break inundation and emergency planning for levees, reservoirs and drainage, and climate adaptation scenarios. Related records: HEC-RAS (model-hec-ras) and ANUGA (model-anuga).
